sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r8/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 38 (batched_criteria_are_scored_independently), Deterministic Checks check-batched-independence-wording.py, Internal Quality Checks row 38 annotation
evidence: All three scored dimensions (weighted_mean) carry explicit independence-and-continue wording and none tells the judge to stop at the first failure. functional/prompt.md:59-61 'Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion.' plus :9 'that criterion fails and scores 0; report what you saw and move on to the next criterion' and :29 'Two failed attempts at the same control fail that criterion; continue.'; functional/judge.toml:6 mode = "individual" (one session per criterion, prompt.md:78 'Each session grades one criterion'), which makes independence structural as well as worded. polish/prompt.md:20-28 '## Independent scoring ... One failed criterion does not zero the others ... mark it failed and continue to every remaining criterion; return a verdict for all of them. The global browser gate is the only all-or-nothing rule'. visual/prompt.md:38-43 same wording with 'mark it with its 0 anchor and continue'. Wording matches/strengthens the frozen template (template functional/prompt.md:68, polish:14-18, visual:44-48). Grep of scored prompts and judge.toml for stop/abort/skip/first fail/remaining/assign 0 found only the sanctioned global browser gate ('If the gate fails, assign 0 to every criterion', functional:18, polish:17, visual:25) and functional:24-25 'when budget runs out, mark the rest failed and say so' — a budget-exhaustion rule, not stop-on-first-failure, and moot per-session in individual mode. Criterion descriptions contain no cross-criterion prerequisites that would let one miss zero another: each functional criterion creates its own JUDGE-* messages (e.g. persistence sets M-12 timer and Sian's wall itself in step b), polish (6 binary) and visual (4 likert) criteria are self-contained. Gates render/constraints are all_pass with 1 criterion each and exempt. Adversarial: a broken app failing e.g. enter_sends still gets independent verdicts for the other 5 polish criteria; a conforming app cannot lose the dimension to one miss. Limits: the private check-batched-independence-wording.py executable is not in the workspace (applied manually per REVIEW_POLICY); raw-evidence-index states no full configured judge run exists, so actual judge compliance is not observed, but this row is a prompt-wording check fully determinable from source.
